prompt: In a random sample of $400$ commuters, $160$ say they bike to work at least once a week. For a $95\%$ confidence interval for the true proportion, using $z^* = 1.96$, what is the margin of error? Round to three decimal places.
hint: A margin of error is a critical value times a standard error. The standard error needs the sample proportion, so find $\hat{p}$ first.

hints.text: A margin of error is a critical value times a standard error. The standard error needs the sample proportion, so find $\hat{p}$ first.
$\hat{p} = 160/400 = 0.40$, so the standard error is $\sqrt{(0.4)(0.6)/400} = \sqrt{0.0006} \approx 0.0245$. Multiply that by $z^* = 1.96$.
$1.96 \times 0.0245 \approx 0.048$, so the margin of error is about $0.048$.

explanation: The sample proportion is the starting point: $\hat{p} = 160/400 = 0.40$.
The standard error measures how much $\hat{p}$ varies: $\sqrt{(0.4)(0.6)/400} = \sqrt{0.0006} \approx 0.0245$.
The margin of error is $z^*$ times the standard error: $1.96 \times 0.0245 \approx 0.048$. The interval is about $0.40 \pm 0.048$, or $(0.352, 0.448)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check the conditions first
steps: Random sample ✓. Successes $160 \ge 10$ and failures $240 \ge 10$ ✓. 400 is surely less than $10\%$ of all commuters ✓.
With conditions met, the one-proportion $z$-interval applies: $\hat{p} \pm z^* \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$.
